text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: kv-cache cardinality spike detected on prod-eu-2. Continuous-batching memory climbed to 92% of node, tail latency > 2s, 5xx rate up ~3.8% for /v1/generate routes using mqa variants (qwen-mqa / mistral-mqa). Auto-throttle did not kick in fast enough. Paging oncall-sre.

oncall-sre: I'm awake, looking. Which customer routes?

incident-bot: top impacted routes: customer-a-chat, customer-b-llm-api. Error signatures: "kv cache OOM" and downstream grpc timeouts to runtime.

cheng: I'm on it. Seeing a KV set growth pattern — keys created per sec jumped x30 in last 10m. Looks like multi-turn chats with function-calls are creating unique prefix keys (GQA->MQA mismatch).

irene: can you confirm model variants? earlier we had a canary for qwen-mqa with batch_max_tokens=2048 rolled last night.

cheng: confirmed. qwen-mqa-canary + mistral-mqa-serving pool both showing same pattern. Likely a change in the encoder that changed prefix hashing, increasing KV cardinality.

sam: quick mitigation idea: lower continuous batching window and force immediate KV eviction for top hot shards. We can also toggle per-tenant batching to single-request mode for the most impacted customers.

lia: on the safety side, customer success pinged two enterprise customers who reported slow responses. CS put them on limited traffic via proxy.

support-engineer: customers seeing increased token cost and timeouts — good to have an ETA on hotfix.

cheng: immediate plan: 1) reduce batching.max_tokens from 2048->512 for the two pools 2) set kv.cache_max_entries temporarily to evict older prefixes (30m->5m) 3) enable fallback model routing to smaller variant (mistral-7b-lite) for affected routes 4) roll these as quick config patches (no model redeploy).

oncall-sre: do we have commands for the hotfix?

cheng: yes, running redwoodctl to push config to the cluster. Commands:

```bash
# reduce batch size
redwoodctl set-config --cluster prod-eu-2 --pool qwen-mqa-canary "batching.max_tokens=512"
redwoodctl set-config --cluster prod-eu-2 --pool mistral-mqa-serving "batching.max_tokens=512"

# lower kv retention
redwoodctl set-config --cluster prod-eu-2 --service kv-cache "kv.cache_max_age=300"

# force eviction on hot shards
redwoodctl admin evict-kv --cluster prod-eu-2 --shard hot-001,hot-002

# enable fallback routing for customer-a and customer-b
redwoodctl route-update --cluster prod-eu-2 --route customer-a-chat --fallback mistral-7b-lite
redwoodctl route-update --cluster prod-eu-2 --route customer-b-llm-api --fallback mistral-7b-lite
```

ire ne: (typo) IRENE: +1 to the plan — make sure to include metrics alarms for downstream latency after change.

sam: I'll prepare a canary before wide rollout — apply to 5% of qwen-mqa traffic then watch 10 min.

lia: I'm updating the incident doc in conj/ops/incidents and pinging CS to tell customers we have an active mitigation.

cheng: executing the change now. Applying batching changes to qwen-mqa-canary (5% first).

incident-bot: deploy-bot: started rolling config update to qwen-mqa-canary at 10:12 UTC.

oncall-sre: saw a drop in cache growth immediately for the canary traffic. Latency back to baseline for canary. 5xxs decreasing.

cheng: good. now applying to remaining nodes in pool with a short stagger (30s).

incident-bot: deploy-bot: updated mistral-mqa-serving pool at 10:19 UTC.

sam: monitoring graphs: node mem usage down from 92% -> 60% across pool, tail latency trending down. Error rate dropping toward baseline.

support-engineer: CS confirmed customer-a sees improvements, customer-b still seeing some timeouts but much reduced.

product-lead: product asked if this was triggered by the decoder change — need a quick RCA note for customers.

cheng: preliminary cause: a combination of changed prefix generation in the new encoder path + high-variance user prompts creating many unique KV keys. The large batch window amplified the problem (many requests combining to create many cache entries before eviction). Essentially a cardinality explosion in KV.

lia: next actions: we should add automated detection for sudden KV key-rate jumps and an emergency auto-evict/rollback policy. Also add per-customer cardinality caps.

oncall-sre: handoff: I'm going offline in 40m. Cheng, can you take the incident for postmortem and follow-ups?

cheng: taking handoff. I'll own the postmortem, RCA, and permanent mitigation roadmap.

incident-bot: summary of actions taken: [batching.max_tokens lowered 2048->512], [kv.cache_max_age 1800->300], [evicted 2 hot shards], [fallback routing enabled for affected customers], [canary first then full rollout].

sam: follow-ups (tickets):
- PROD-INC-4678: add KV cardinality monitoring + auto-evict rule
- PROD-INC-4679: add per-tenant kv entry caps + opt-out routing
- PROD-INC-4680: test suite for GQA vs MQA prefix compatibility on encoder changes

support-engineer: customer communication: drafted status update to affected customers (waiting on product approval).

product-lead: approved. send now. keep me in loop for the postmortem.

cheng: creating postmortem draft and will include timelines, root cause hypothesis, and code/config changes. Will also include a rollback gating improvement for batch config changes.

lia: nice work everyone. Marking incident as mitigated for now. We'll keep monitoring for 6 hours.

incident-bot: incident resolved flag suggested by oncall-sre at 10:45 UTC. Monitoring window set 6h.

cheng: handoff note: follow-ups assigned, I'll drive the RCA and coordinate a patch to make batch window adaptive based on cardinality signals.

oncall-sre: closing shift — leave notes in the incident doc. Thanks. :thumbsup:

(End of thread)
